Every morning, the same question. Where do we actually stand?
Until now, the answer lived in a spreadsheet. Somebody had to open it, scroll it, and work it out. Most mornings, nobody did.
Ten minutes of scrolling, for a number that was already out of date by lunchtime. Now it is one glance.
So we built the wall. One screen. Seven slides. Running by itself.
It opens on the only number that matters before any other. How many people are waiting to hear from us right now. Every one of them was promised a person, not an auto reply.
Then the day. What came in this morning, what has come in this month, and what the branch has actually closed.
Then the team. Every agent, ranked by what they have finished, not by what they were handed. Clients the branch assigned. Clients they brought in themselves. Both counted. Never mixed together.
Then what is waiting on us. Oldest first. Anything past the day we promised turns red, and it stays red until somebody handles it.
Thirty days of filings, so you can see the rhythm. The quiet weeks show up as clearly as the busy ones, and the line only climbs.
Then it goes live. Reviews landing. Links being opened. Somebody asking to be called back. It changes while you are standing in front of it.
And it finishes on the promise. How much of it we kept. If anything is late, the wall says so, in front of everybody.
It runs itself. Put it on a screen, leave it there, and the branch can watch itself work. Don't have an agent dot com, slash wall.
